actions.decision_timing: contemporaneous owner semantic review of OLP-0045 against its cut definition, completeness proof, rational embedding, and claimed total real operations

actions.decision_timing: contemporaneous owner semantic review of OLP-0045 against its cut definition, completeness proof, rational embedding, and claimed total real operations
actions.translation_change: preserves all active cases and the inactive zero rule, but records that the active piecewise definition omits products with one zero factor and one negative factor
actions.counterexample: If alpha is zero and beta is negative, the nonnegative case fails because beta is not nonnegative, and all three signed cases fail because alpha is neither positive nor negative.
actions.formula_policy: Frozen active and commented formulas remain authoritative; the missing active cases are disclosed, not invented.

actions.decision_timing: contemporaneous owner semantic review of OLP-0047 against the earlier quotient constructions, the stated algebraic definitions, and the active versus commented cut operations
actions.translation_change: preserves the ring calculations but records that the source has not first proved that operations on integer and rational equivalence classes are independent of representative choice
actions.counterexample: Without representative independence, replacing one pair by an equivalent pair could change a purported sum or product class, so the later ring-law calculations would not yet define operations.
actions.formula_policy: Every source formula is preserved; the missing logical prerequisite is disclosed in prose.

actions.decision_timing: contemporaneous owner semantic review of OLP-0047 against the earlier quotient constructions, the stated algebraic definitions, and the active versus commented cut operations
actions.translation_change: supplies the missing noun “task” in the phrase describing the tedious task of checking the ordered-field laws
actions.counterexample: The frozen phrase “run through the (tedious) of checking” is grammatically incomplete and its intended object is fixed by the surrounding sentence.
actions.formula_policy: No formula changes; this is a prose-only completion.

actions.decision_timing: contemporaneous owner semantic review of OLP-0047 against the earlier quotient constructions, the stated algebraic definitions, and the active versus commented cut operations
actions.translation_change: preserves the displayed definition but records that the conventional field definition also requires zero and one to be distinct
actions.counterexample: In the zero ring, the quantified inverse clause is vacuously true because there are no nonzero elements, so the written definition admits the trivial ring as a field.
actions.formula_policy: The frozen displayed axiom is unchanged; the omitted conventional hypothesis is disclosed.

actions.decision_timing: contemporaneous owner semantic review of OLP-0047 against the earlier quotient constructions, the stated algebraic definitions, and the active versus commented cut operations
actions.translation_change: preserves the request to check subtraction and division as cuts but records that the only formulas for those operations are inactive comments in the preceding source section
actions.counterexample: A reader cannot verify that an operation always yields a cut before the operation has an active definition; the later ordered-field exercise also depends on division or multiplicative inverses.
actions.formula_policy: Active and commented source formulas remain frozen; no missing definition is invented.

actions.decision_timing: contemporaneous owner semantic review of OLP-0048 against its quotient definition, constant-sequence embedding, order type, ordered-field claim, and completeness proof
actions.translation_change: identifies real numbers with equivalence classes, rather than with the equivalence relation itself, matching the source definition immediately below
actions.counterexample: Realequiv is one binary relation on the collection of Cauchy sequences, whereas each real constructed here is one of its many equivalence classes; these have different types.
actions.formula_policy: The defining relation and quotient formulas are unchanged; the prose type is corrected.

actions.decision_timing: contemporaneous owner semantic review of OLP-0048 against its quotient definition, constant-sequence embedding, order type, ordered-field claim, and completeness proof
actions.translation_change: preserves the exercise symbol sim subscript Real but records that the relation defined just above is Realequiv, rendered by a different symbol
actions.counterexample: The section introduces no definition equating sim subscript Real with Realequiv, so the exercise notation is formally unbound even though the intended equivalence is clear.
actions.formula_policy: The frozen exercise formula is unchanged; the intended referent is disclosed in prose.

actions.decision_timing: contemporaneous owner semantic review of OLP-0048 against its quotient definition, constant-sequence embedding, order type, ordered-field claim, and completeness proof
actions.translation_change: changes zero subscript Rat to zero subscript Real in the positivity test because the left operand is a real equivalence class and rational embeddings were defined with the Real subscript
actions.counterexample: The section defines q subscript Real as a constant-sequence class. Zero subscript Rat is a rational from the preceding construction and is not the same typed object as equivrep(f).
actions.formula_policy: Only the ill-typed subscript is corrected; the eventual-positivity quantifier is unchanged.

actions.decision_timing: contemporaneous owner semantic review of OLP-0048 against its quotient definition, constant-sequence embedding, order type, ordered-field claim, and completeness proof
actions.translation_change: states both the ordered-field and completeness results for Realequiv equivalence classes rather than for unquotiented Cauchy sequences
actions.counterexample: Distinct null sequences would be distinct additive-zero candidates before quotienting, and pointwise inversion is not defined for every raw nonzero Cauchy sequence. The quotient classes are the reals on which the preceding operations and order were defined.
actions.formula_policy: No displayed formula changes; theorem and exercise prose are corrected to the defined carrier.

actions.decision_timing: contemporaneous owner semantic review of OLP-0048 against its quotient definition, constant-sequence embedding, order type, ordered-field claim, and completeness proof
actions.translation_change: preserves the rational bisection construction but records that choosing rational upper and lower endpoints from an arbitrary real bound and member requires an unproved Archimedean or rational-density lemma for the newly constructed reals
actions.counterexample: Nonemptiness and existence of some real upper bound alone do not syntactically provide p and q in Rat. Their existence follows only after proving that embedded rationals are cofinal and coinitial, or an equivalent Archimedean result.
actions.formula_policy: All bisection formulas are unchanged; the omitted prerequisite is disclosed in prose.

actions.decision_timing: contemporaneous owner semantic review of the complete infinite-set chapter against function typing, the stated closure properties, and the proof that applies the helper proposition
actions.translation_change: preserves the displayed closure definition but records that the phrase “any function” and the range-union example require an endofunction on an ambient domain containing every considered set
actions.counterexample: For a function with domain {0} and value f(0)=1, the set ran(f) union {0} contains 1 although f(1) is undefined, so it is not f-closed under the displayed unrestricted wording.
actions.formula_policy: Every frozen formula is preserved; the missing typing hypothesis is disclosed in prose.

actions.decision_timing: contemporaneous owner semantic review of the complete infinite-set chapter against function typing, the stated closure properties, and the proof that applies the helper proposition
actions.translation_change: replaces the nested cardinal-equality macro with A equinumerous with B, the exact conclusion proved by the constructed bijection from A to B and required by the later squeeze application
actions.counterexample: The source feeds a cardinal-equality proposition as the first set argument of another cardinal equality, which is not a well-typed set-size statement. The proof explicitly ends with a bijection A to B.
actions.formula_policy: Only the malformed conclusion formula is corrected; all hypotheses and proof formulas are unchanged.

actions.decision_timing: contemporaneous owner review of the complete propositional syntax and semantics chapter against its inductive grammar, syntactic-identity definition, truth tables and fixed-formula theorem scopes
actions.translation_change: removes the unmatched closing parenthesis after the disjunction-based expansion of the conditional; the resulting formula is the standard not-A-or-B abbreviation stated by the source branch
actions.counterexample: The source branch contains a closing parenthesis without a matching opening parenthesis, so the displayed abbreviation is not a well-formed formula string under the chapter’s own grammar.
actions.formula_policy: Only the unmatched closing parenthesis is removed; the alternative conjunction-based expansion is unchanged.

actions.decision_timing: contemporaneous owner review of the complete propositional syntax and semantics chapter against its inductive grammar, syntactic-identity definition, truth tables and fixed-formula theorem scopes
actions.translation_change: replaces semantic equivalence with syntactic identity in the conjunction case of the converse formation-sequence proof, matching the definition and every parallel connective case
actions.counterexample: Semantically equivalent formulas need not be the same symbol string; for example, commuted conjunctions can agree in truth value while having distinct formation strings. The proof needs the final sequence entry to be exactly the displayed conjunction.
actions.formula_policy: Only the relation symbol in the malformed proof sentence is corrected; all formula components are unchanged.

actions.decision_timing: contemporaneous owner review of the complete propositional syntax and semantics chapter against its inductive grammar, syntactic-identity definition, truth tables and fixed-formula theorem scopes
actions.translation_change: renders the second statement of the local-determination hypothesis as referring to variables occurring in the already fixed formula A, consistent with the first statement and conclusion
actions.counterexample: If “some formula” introduced an unrelated existential formula, agreement on a variable appearing elsewhere would not ensure agreement on every variable of the fixed formula whose value is compared.
actions.formula_policy: No formula or identifier is changed; only the scope-bearing prose is clarified.

actions.decision_timing: contemporaneous owner review of the complete proof-systems overview against the stated sequent syntax, independent side sequences, tableau rule-label convention and displayed examples
actions.translation_change: changes the right sequence’s terminal subscript from m to n so the left and right finite sequences may have independent lengths, as the surrounding definition and empty-side cases require
actions.counterexample: Using m on both sides makes the displayed schema require equal-length sequences and makes it impossible for exactly one side to be empty, contradicting the next sentence and later root sequents.
actions.formula_policy: Only the right terminal index is changed from m to n; all sentence variables, order, punctuation and sequent symbol are preserved.
